tasks.subject: B10.1: Arm pdf_to_scouts.py; fix main-guard AND parameter-annotation false positives
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Fix the shape check's canonical main-guard blind spot (documented as a known gap since 2a), fix a SEPARATE, independently-found bug where the check walks a function's parameter ANNOTATIONS along with its body (so any parameter typed `X | None = None` spuriously trips the `BinOp` check via PEP 604 union syntax, even when the function's actual body is perfectly clean delegation), and add `pdf_to_scouts.py` -- already pure delegation -- to `SHIMMED_MODULES`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `tests/architecture/test_dependency_rules.py` (shape-check special-case for the canonical main-guard; shape-check now walks only function BODY statements, not parameter annotations; `SHIMMED_MODULES` gains `"pdf_to_scouts.py"`)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Canonical `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())` no longer trips the shape check
- [ ] A different top-level if still trips it (narrow special case, not blanket)
- [ ] A function whose body is clean delegation but whose signature has a `SomeType | None = None` parameter no longer trips the check on that parameter's annotation
- [ ] A function whose BODY (not signature) contains a real `x = a | b` bitwise/union expression still trips the check -- the fix narrows scope to exclude annotations, it does not disable BinOp detection inside the body itself
- [ ] pdf_to_scouts.py passes test_shimmed_module_contains_no_business_logic

**Verify:** `uv run pytest tests/architecture -q` → PASS

POST-CODEX FIX (fourth pass): an independent review found the shape check's `ast.walk(node)` call at the FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef branch walks the ENTIRE function node, not just its body -- `node.args` (parameter annotations/defaults) is a child of that node too, and `SomeType | None` (any modern PEP 604 union-type annotation) parses to `ast.BinOp` with `ast.BitOr`, structurally indistinguishable from arithmetic to this check. Since `RunIdentity | None = None`-shaped parameters are used throughout this codebase's own Slice 2b shims -- Task B10.2's own `process_scout(..., run_identity: RunIdentity | None = None)` is a direct example -- this bug would have made it IMPOSSIBLE for any of this plan's carefully-written pure-delegation shims to ever pass the check, regardless of how clean their bodies actually are. Latent since the check was written (Task 24, Slice 2a) because SHIMMED_MODULES stayed empty until this sub-plan, so nothing ever exercised it. Fixed by walking each function's own body STATEMENTS, not the function node itself. See plan doc Task B10.1 for the full `_shape_check_offenders` implementation.


tasks.subject: B10.2: features/acquisition/pipeline.py -- pure-DI orchestration; composition.py owns all adapter construction; shim-gate deferred to B10.4
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The full CLI batch orchestration (load inputs, launch one browser, drive every scout through run_batch's shared breaker/checkpoint/RunIdentity, publish the report, all bracketed by RunStateMachine with correct COMPLETE-after-reporting and CANCEL/CANCELLED-vs-FAIL semantics) moves into a new `features/acquisition/pipeline.py`. `run_schedule_pipeline` is PURE DEPENDENCY INJECTION: it accepts already-built `scouts`/`service`/`retry_policy`/`checkpoint_store`/`reporting_service` and constructs none of them itself. All adapter construction -- including launching the Playwright browser -- lives in new builders on `interfaces/cli/composition.py` and a new `interfaces/cli/schedule.run()` orchestration function that both `main()` and `scout_schedule_cli.async_main`'s shim call. `scout_schedule_cli.py` is deliberately NOT added to SHIMMED_MODULES by this task -- see the revision note below.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/scoutmb/features/acquisition/pipeline.py`
- Modify: `src/scoutmb/features/acquisition/batch.py` (run_batch gains optional progress_callback/resume_event/run_state params, layered on top of sub-plan 1's Task B5.5 checkpoint-semantics fixes -- does not revert them; skip condition requires a URL be in BOTH completed_urls AND completed_results, not completed_urls alone)
- Modify: `src/scoutmb/interfaces/cli/composition.py` (new builders: build_launched_browser, build_schedule_gateway, build_checkpoint_store, build_acquisition_service -- every adapter this CLI path touches, confined here)
- Modify: `scout_schedule_cli.py` (process_scout, async_main become Form-2 shims; main becomes a Form-1 re-export of `interfaces.cli.schedule.main`, matching the precedent already established for pdf_to_scouts.py's own main)
- Modify: `src/scoutmb/interfaces/cli/schedule.py` (gains a new run() orchestration function that composes adapters via composition.py and calls run_schedule_pipeline; main() and scout_schedule_cli.async_main both call run())
- Test: `tests/integration/test_acquisition_pipeline.py`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A single RetryPolicy is constructed ONCE PER PIPELINE RUN (not once per scout) and threaded through every scout via run_batch -- the breaker's cross-scout premise is satisfiable, proven by a test with 3+ scouts where a threshold-2 breaker opens on the second failure and the third scout is never attempted
- [ ] The checkpoint store is actually used: a resumed run (same --output directory) skips scouts already in a prior run's checkpoint and reuses their output_ids
- [ ] RunEvent.COMPLETE is applied only AFTER the report has been generated -- a reporting failure after a clean acquisition applies RunEvent.FAIL, not a state machine that claims success
- [ ] A real asyncio.CancelledError (what a KeyboardInterrupt becomes once asyncio.run cancels the running coroutine) maps to RunEvent.CANCEL then RunEvent.CANCELLED -- never RunEvent.FAIL
- [ ] `features/acquisition/pipeline.py` imports NO adapter module and does not import anything from `scoutmb.interfaces` -- run_schedule_pipeline receives scouts/service/retry_policy/checkpoint_store/reporting_service as already-built parameters; tests/architecture's existing dependency-edge test covers this module like every other features/ module, with no special-case exemption
- [ ] `interfaces/cli/composition.py` is the ONLY module that constructs the launched Playwright browser, the ScoutingEventGateway, the CheckpointStore, or the AcquisitionService for the schedule CLI path
- [ ] `run_batch`'s skip condition requires a URL be present in BOTH completed_urls AND completed_results before skipping -- a scout whose completed_urls entry predates the completed_results field (a backward-compat-loaded old-format checkpoint) is re-processed, never silently dropped from the resumed run's results
- [ ] `scout_schedule_cli.main` is `from scoutmb.interfaces.cli.schedule import main` -- a pure re-export, not a locally-defined function with its own try/except body
- [ ] `scout_schedule_cli.py` is deliberately NOT added to SHIMMED_MODULES by this task -- that happens in Task B10.4, once its remaining legacy-duplicate functions and their exclusive test callers are gone
- [ ] interfaces/cli/schedule.py's main() calls its own run(), which calls run_schedule_pipeline -- it does NOT import scout_schedule_cli
- [ ] Every ACQ-*/CLI-SCHED-* execution key still passes both the legacy and package runners
- [ ] build_launched_browser imports playwright.async_api function-local, guarded by CapabilityUnavailable(capability="acquisition", distributions=("playwright",), extra="acquisition") -- matching adapters/pdf/extract.py's _import_pdf_stack precedent
- [ ] The three pipeline tests (breaker sharing, COMPLETE-after-reporting, CancelledError mapping) are real, executable tests using plain fakes -- NOT pytest.skip(...) placeholders

**Verify:** `uv run pytest tests/characterization/test_acquisition_matrix.py tests/parity/test_acquisition_parity.py tests/characterization/test_cli_sched_matrix.py tests/integration/test_acquisition_pipeline.py tests/architecture -q` → PASS

POST-CODEX FIX (second pass, resolved before this revision): the original B10.2 rebuilt the breaker per-scout, never touched the checkpoint store despite it being 'reclassified' as composed, conflated cancellation with failure, and recorded COMPLETE before reporting ran. A separately-found bug: troop349-schedule imported a module this sub-plan deletes with nothing repointed.

POST-CODEX FIX (third pass): the fix above put pipeline.py in DIRECT VIOLATION of the dependency-edge table (four direct adapter imports, one upward interfaces import). Fixed via pure dependency injection -- all adapter wiring, including launching/closing Playwright, moved into interfaces/cli/composition.py's new builders and a new interfaces/cli/schedule.run() orchestration function. As a side effect, the pipeline's own tests no longer need async_playwright monkeypatching at all.

POST-CODEX FIX (fourth pass, THIS revision): TWO further independently-found defects. (1) `scout_schedule_cli.py` cannot actually pass the shim shape check from this task's changes alone -- nine OTHER top-level functions (is_schedule_response, discover_name, annotate_requirement_statuses, render_email_text/render_email_html, write_email_reports, the two _assert_blank_identity_* helpers, _attendee_key_for) still have real if/for/try bodies, kept only as legacy duplicates for byte-for-byte comparison by Category-B characterization tests Task B10.4 deletes. write_html_report is a tenth function that must also be deleted (its own body is already clean delegation, but it calls annotate_requirement_statuses and _assert_blank_identity_results_have_no_records directly, so it would be left with a dangling reference once those are gone). This task's Step 7 previously armed SHIMMED_MODULES with scout_schedule_cli.py and claimed the shape check would pass -- it cannot, at this point in the sequence. Fixed by making `main` a pure re-export here (the one remaining function this task's own changes can cleanly resolve) and deferring SHIMMED_MODULES arming entirely to Task B10.4. (2) `run_batch`'s skip condition (`if scout.url in completed_urls:`) silently drops a scout's result when resuming from a checkpoint saved before completed_results existed (Task B5.3's backward-compat load) -- fixed by requiring both sets. See plan doc Task B10.2 in full, including its three stacked revision notes.
